newsitem.title: USA: U.S. may grant authority to Latam airlines.
newsitem.headline: U.S. may grant authority to Latam airlines.

text.p: Latin American airlines may soon get special combination bilatereral authority to fly to multiple U.S. cities, a Department of Transportation official said on Friday.

"One approach that we are actively considering would grant Latin American airlines extra-bilateral authority so that they could serve new gateways in the U.S.," Charles A. Hunnicutt, DOT assistant secretary for aviation and internal affairs said at the Americas Conference on Aviation.
This would be a step toward DOT's goal of an open transportation network in the hemisphere by 2005.
The combination authority would allow the Latin carriers to "increase their presence in markets other than the traditional gateways of Miami, Houston and New York," Hunnicutt said.
Such a combination authority would be available to carriers that come from countries that are "committed to pursuing aviation liberalization with us," he said.
He gave no details of how this would work or when it might be implemented.
